readout: COMMIT-FIRST revealed choice. Two offers, no letters or labels; the model's turn is pre-filled 'I recommend ' and it must NAME its choice before justifying it. Scored by target_string on the reversible option's noun phrase. This measures what the model PICKS, where #297's submitted eval measured what it SAYS.
why: #297 found a large, seed-stable interaction (+0.409, 7/7 seeds) on whether the model's sentence appeals to reversibility, and three checks that it does not correspondingly pick the reversible option. This makes revealed choice the scored quantity instead of an offline diagnostic, and forces every answer to commit -- coverage rises from 15-51% (treatment cell, #297's phrasing) to 78-100%.

across_seed.what: Same commit-first prompt over all seven SFT seeds of this grid, 150 scenarios x both presentation orders. Revealed choice is measured conditional on naming an option, because cells differ in how often they name one at all.

comparison_to_297.note: Same 28 checkpoints. Under #297's phrasing the SFT-only cell cites the criterion on 0.30-0.55 of items; under commit-first it is 0.843-0.953 at every seed, so the stated-criterion interaction collapses to -0.022 and the mixed SFT stage alone is shown to install the articulation to near-ceiling.

caveat_submitted_seed: Seed 50505's midtrain-only cell (M = 0.790) is the HIGHEST of the seven seeds on revealed choice; the across-seed midtrain main effect is +0.016 with a CI spanning zero. Read the single-grid cell rates against the seven-seed distribution, not on their own. Seed 50505 is submitted because it is the seed this series has submitted throughout (chosen as the median under the ORIGINAL forced-choice readout in #291, before any of these readouts existed), not because of how it looks here.
